answer:
The tape’s scale factor is

\[
\frac{\text{true length}}{\text{tape reading}}=\frac{102}{100}=1.02.
\]

So both floor dimensions must be multiplied by \(1.02\), and area by \(1.02^2\):

\[
A_{\text{uncorrected}}=380\cdot260\text{ cm}^2=98{,}800\text{ cm}^2=9.88\text{ m}^2,
\]

\[
A_{\text{true}}=9.88(1.02)^2=10.279152\text{ m}^2\approx 10.28\text{ m}^2.
\]

Using the true area as the denominator, the quoted uncorrected area has signed percentage error

\[
\frac{A_{\text{uncorrected}}-A_{\text{true}}}{A_{\text{true}}}\times100\%
=
\frac{9.88-10.279152}{10.279152}\times100\%
\approx -3.883\%.
\]

Thus:

- True area: \(\boxed{\approx 10.28\ \text{m}^2}\) (more exactly \(10.279152\ \text{m}^2\)).
- Signed percentage error of the uncorrected quoted area, using true area as denominator:  
  \[
  \boxed{-3.88\%\approx -3.9\%}
  \]
  (the uncorrected quoted area is too small).

If instead the uncorrected/quoted area is used as the denominator, the signed error would be \(-4.04\%\).
